steps: To determine the ancestral state of a trait among closely related species, biologists use the outgroup method.
An outgroup is a more distantly related organism that serves as a reference group.
Option A is unhelpful because no fossils exist.
Option C uses a mammal, which is too distantly related to provide useful information about a snake-specific trait.
Option B correctly describes finding a more distantly related snake (an outgroup) to compare the trait, which is the standard phylogenetic approach.
